126: add_dir(Name, Job=[Dir|_Dirs]) when is_list(Dir) ->
127:     add_job(cast_to_list(Name),
128: 	    lists:map(fun(D)-> {dir,cast_to_list(D)} end, Job));
129: add_dir(Name, Dir) ->
130:     add_job(cast_to_list(Name), {dir,cast_to_list(Dir)}).
131: 
132: add_dir(Name, Job=[Dir|_Dirs], Pattern) when is_list(Dir) ->
133:     add_job(cast_to_list(Name),
134: 	    lists:map(fun(D)-> {dir,cast_to_list(D),
135: 				cast_to_list(Pattern)} end, Job));
136: add_dir(Name, Dir, Pattern) ->
137:     add_job(cast_to_list(Name), {dir,cast_to_list(Dir),cast_to_list(Pattern)}).
138: 
139: add_module(Mod) when is_atom(Mod) ->
140:     add_job(atom_to_list(Mod), {Mod,all}).
141: 
142: add_module(Name, Mods) when is_list(Mods) ->
143:     add_job(cast_to_list(Name), lists:map(fun(Mod) -> {Mod,all} end, Mods)).
144: 
145: add_conf(Name, Mod, Conf) when is_tuple(Conf) ->
146:     add_job(cast_to_list(Name), {Mod,[Conf]});
147: 
148: add_conf(Name, Mod, Confs) when is_list(Confs) ->
149:     add_job(cast_to_list(Name), {Mod,Confs}).
150: 
151: add_case(Mod, Case) when is_atom(Mod), is_atom(Case) ->
152:     add_job(atom_to_list(Mod), {Mod,Case}).
153: 
154: add_case(Name, Mod, Case) when is_atom(Mod), is_atom(Case) ->
155:     add_job(Name, {Mod,Case}).
156: 
157: add_cases(Mod, Cases) when is_atom(Mod), is_list(Cases) ->
158:     add_job(atom_to_list(Mod), {Mod,Cases}).
159: 
160: add_cases(Name, Mod, Cases) when is_atom(Mod), is_list(Cases) ->
161:     add_job(Name, {Mod,Cases}).
162: 
163: add_spec(Spec) ->
164:     Name = filename:rootname(Spec, ".spec"),
165:     case filelib:is_file(Spec) of
166: 	true -> add_job(Name, {spec,Spec});
167: 	false -> {error,nofile}
168:     end.
169: 
170: %% This version of the interface is to be used if there are
171: %% suites or cases that should be skipped.
172: 
173: add_dir_with_skip(Name, Job=[Dir|_Dirs], Skip) when is_list(Dir) ->
174:     add_job(cast_to_list(Name),
175: 	    lists:map(fun(D)-> {dir,cast_to_list(D)} end, Job),
176: 	    Skip);
177: add_dir_with_skip(Name, Dir, Skip) ->
178:     add_job(cast_to_list(Name), {dir,cast_to_list(Dir)}, Skip).
179: 
180: add_dir_with_skip(Name, Job=[Dir|_Dirs], Pattern, Skip) when is_list(Dir) ->
181:     add_job(cast_to_list(Name),
182: 	    lists:map(fun(D)-> {dir,cast_to_list(D),
183: 				cast_to_list(Pattern)} end, Job),
184: 	    Skip);
185: add_dir_with_skip(Name, Dir, Pattern, Skip) ->
186:     add_job(cast_to_list(Name),
187: 	    {dir,cast_to_list(Dir),cast_to_list(Pattern)}, Skip).
188: 
189: add_module_with_skip(Mod, Skip) when is_atom(Mod) ->
190:     add_job(atom_to_list(Mod), {Mod,all}, Skip).
191: 
192: add_module_with_skip(Name, Mods, Skip) when is_list(Mods) ->
193:     add_job(cast_to_list(Name), lists:map(fun(Mod) -> {Mod,all} end, Mods), Skip).
194: 
195: add_conf_with_skip(Name, Mod, Conf, Skip) when is_tuple(Conf) ->
196:     add_job(cast_to_list(Name), {Mod,[Conf]}, Skip);
197: 
198: add_conf_with_skip(Name, Mod, Confs, Skip) when is_list(Confs) ->
199:     add_job(cast_to_list(Name), {Mod,Confs}, Skip).
200: 
201: add_case_with_skip(Mod, Case, Skip) when is_atom(Mod), is_atom(Case) ->
202:     add_job(atom_to_list(Mod), {Mod,Case}, Skip).
203: 
204: add_case_with_skip(Name, Mod, Case, Skip) when is_atom(Mod), is_atom(Case) ->
205:     add_job(Name, {Mod,Case}, Skip).
206: 
207: add_cases_with_skip(Mod, Cases, Skip) when is_atom(Mod), is_list(Cases) ->
208:     add_job(atom_to_list(Mod), {Mod,Cases}, Skip).
209: 
210: add_cases_with_skip(Name, Mod, Cases, Skip) when is_atom(Mod), is_list(Cases) ->
211:     add_job(Name, {Mod,Cases}, Skip).
212: 
213: add_tests_with_skip(LogDir, Tests, Skip) ->
214:     add_job(LogDir,
215: 	    lists:map(fun({Dir,all,all}) ->
216: 			      {Dir,{dir,Dir}};
217: 			 ({Dir,Mods,all}) ->
218: 			      {Dir,lists:map(fun(M) -> {M,all} end, Mods)};
219: 			 ({Dir,Mod,Cases}) ->
220: 			      {Dir,{Mod,Cases}}
221: 		      end, Tests),
222: 	    Skip).

225: %% COMMAND LINE INTERFACE
226: 
227: parse_cmd_line(Cmds) ->
228:     parse_cmd_line(Cmds, [], [], local, false, undefined).
229: 
230: parse_cmd_line(['SPEC',Spec|Cmds], SpecList, Names, Param, Cov, TCCB) ->
231:     case file:consult(Spec) of
232: 	{ok, TermList} ->
233: 	    Name = filename:rootname(Spec),
234: 	    parse_cmd_line(Cmds, TermList++SpecList, [Name|Names], Param,
235: 			   Cov, TCCB);
236: 	{error,Reason} ->
237: 	    io:format("Can't open ~tw: ~tp\n",[Spec, file:format_error(Reason)]),
238: 	    parse_cmd_line(Cmds, SpecList, Names, Param, Cov, TCCB)
239:     end;
240: parse_cmd_line(['NAME',Name|Cmds], SpecList, Names, Param, Cov, TCCB) ->
241:     parse_cmd_line(Cmds, SpecList, [{name,atom_to_list(Name)}|Names],
242: 		   Param, Cov, TCCB);
243: parse_cmd_line(['SKIPMOD',Mod|Cmds], SpecList, Names, Param, Cov, TCCB) ->
244:     parse_cmd_line(Cmds, [{skip,{Mod,"by command line"}}|SpecList], Names,
245: 		   Param, Cov, TCCB);
246: parse_cmd_line(['SKIPCASE',Mod,Case|Cmds], SpecList, Names, Param, Cov, TCCB) ->
247:     parse_cmd_line(Cmds, [{skip,{Mod,Case,"by command line"}}|SpecList], Names,
248: 		   Param, Cov, TCCB);
249: parse_cmd_line(['DIR',Dir|Cmds], SpecList, Names, Param, Cov, TCCB) ->
250:     Name = filename:basename(Dir),
251:     parse_cmd_line(Cmds, [{topcase,{dir,Name}}|SpecList], [Name|Names],
252: 		   Param, Cov, TCCB);
253: parse_cmd_line(['MODULE',Mod|Cmds], SpecList, Names, Param, Cov, TCCB) ->
254:     parse_cmd_line(Cmds,[{topcase,{Mod,all}}|SpecList],[atom_to_list(Mod)|Names],
255: 		   Param, Cov, TCCB);
256: parse_cmd_line(['CASE',Mod,Case|Cmds], SpecList, Names, Param, Cov, TCCB) ->
257:     parse_cmd_line(Cmds,[{topcase,{Mod,Case}}|SpecList],[atom_to_list(Mod)|Names],
258: 		   Param, Cov, TCCB);
259: parse_cmd_line(['COVER',App,CF,Analyse|Cmds], SpecList, Names, Param, _Cov, TCCB) ->
260:     parse_cmd_line(Cmds, SpecList, Names, Param, {{App,CF}, Analyse}, TCCB);
261: parse_cmd_line(['TESTCASE_CALLBACK',Mod,Func|Cmds], SpecList, Names, Param, Cov, _) ->
262:     parse_cmd_line(Cmds, SpecList, Names, Param, Cov, {Mod,Func});
263: parse_cmd_line([Obj|_Cmds], _SpecList, _Names, _Param, __Cov, _TCCB) ->
264:     io:format("~w: Bad argument: ~tw\n", [?MODULE,Obj]),
265:     io:format(" Use the `ts' module to start tests.\n", []),
266:     io:format(" (If you ARE using `ts', there is a bug in `ts'.)\n", []),
267:     halt(1);
268: parse_cmd_line([], SpecList, Names, Param, Cov, TCCB) ->
269:     NameList = lists:reverse(Names, ["suite"]),
270:     Name = case lists:keysearch(name, 1, NameList) of
271: 	       {value,{name,N}} -> N;
272: 	       false -> hd(NameList)
273: 	   end,
274:     {lists:reverse(SpecList), Name, Param, Cov, TCCB}.

311: run_test(CommandLine) ->
312:     process_flag(trap_exit,true),
313:     {SpecList,Name,Param,Cov,TCCB} = parse_cmd_line(CommandLine),
314:     {ok,_TSPid} = start_link(Param),
315:     case Cov of
316: 	false -> ok;
317: 	{{App,CoverFile},Analyse} -> cover(App, maybe_file(CoverFile), Analyse)
318:     end,
319:     testcase_callback(TCCB),
320:     add_job(Name, {command_line,SpecList}),
321: 
322:     wait_finish().

326:     none;
327: maybe_file(CoverFile) ->

348: 	    ok

491:     case init:get_argument(test_server_format_exception) of
492: 	{ok,[[TSFE]]} ->

494: 	_ ->
495: 	    ok
496:     end,
497:     test_server_sup:cleanup_crash_dumps(),
498:     test_server_sup:util_start(),
499:     State = #state{jobs=[],finish=false},
500:     TI0 = test_server:init_target_info(),

504: 			 master=TargetHost},
505:     _ = ets:new(slave_tab, [named_table,set,public,{keypos,2}]),

553: %% Skip = [SkipItem]
554: %% SkipItem = {Mod,Comment} | {Mod,Case,Comment} | {Mod,Cases,Comment}
555: %% Mod = Case = atom()
556: %% Comment = string()
557: %% Cases = [Case]
558: %%
559: %% Adds a job to the job queue. The name of the job is Name. A log directory
560: %% will be created in Dir/Name.logs. TopCase may be anything that
561: %% collect_cases/3 accepts, plus the following:
562: %%
563: %% {spec,SpecName} executes the named test suite specification file. Commands
564: %% in the file should be in the format accepted by do_spec_list/1.
565: %%
566: %% {command_line,SpecList} executes the list of specification instructions
567: %% supplied, which should be in the format accepted by do_spec_list/1.
568: 
569: handle_call({add_job,Dir,Name,TopCase,Skip}, _From, State) ->
570:     LogDir = Dir ++ ?logdir_ext,
571:     ExtraTools =
572: 	case State#state.cover of
573: 	    false -> [];
574: 	    CoverInfo -> [{cover,CoverInfo}]
575: 	end,
576:     ExtraTools1 =
577: 	case State#state.random_seed of
578: 	    undefined -> ExtraTools;
579: 	    Seed -> [{random_seed,Seed}|ExtraTools]
580: 	end,
581:     case lists:keysearch(Name, 1, State#state.jobs) of
582: 	false ->
583: 	    case TopCase of
584: 		{spec,SpecName} ->
585: 		    Pid = spawn_tester(
586: 			    ?MODULE, do_spec,
587: 			    [SpecName,{State#state.multiply_timetraps,
588: 				       State#state.scale_timetraps}],
589: 			    LogDir, Name, State#state.levels,
590: 			    State#state.reject_io_reqs,
591: 			    State#state.create_priv_dir,
592: 			    State#state.testcase_callback, ExtraTools1),
593: 		    NewJobs = [{Name,Pid}|State#state.jobs],
594: 		    {reply, ok, State#state{jobs=NewJobs}};
595: 		{command_line,SpecList} ->
596: 		    Pid = spawn_tester(
597: 			    ?MODULE, do_spec_list,
598: 			    [SpecList,{State#state.multiply_timetraps,
599: 				       State#state.scale_timetraps}],
600: 			    LogDir, Name, State#state.levels,
601: 			    State#state.reject_io_reqs,
602: 			    State#state.create_priv_dir,
603: 			    State#state.testcase_callback, ExtraTools1),
604: 		    NewJobs = [{Name,Pid}|State#state.jobs],
605: 		    {reply, ok, State#state{jobs=NewJobs}};
606: 		TopCase ->
607: 		    case State#state.get_totals of
608: 			{CliPid,Fun} ->
609: 			    Result = count_test_cases(TopCase, Skip),
610: 			    Fun(CliPid, Result),
611: 			    {reply, ok, State};
612: 			_ ->
613: 			    Cfg = make_config([]),
614: 			    Pid = spawn_tester(
615: 				    ?MODULE, do_test_cases,
616: 				    [TopCase,Skip,Cfg,
617: 				     {State#state.multiply_timetraps,
618: 				      State#state.scale_timetraps}],
619: 				    LogDir, Name, State#state.levels,
620: 				    State#state.reject_io_reqs,
621: 				    State#state.create_priv_dir,
622: 				    State#state.testcase_callback, ExtraTools1),
623: 			    NewJobs = [{Name,Pid}|State#state.jobs],
624: 			    {reply, ok, State#state{jobs=NewJobs}}
625: 		    end
626: 	    end;
627: 	_ ->
628: 	    {reply,{error,name_already_in_use},State}
629:     end;

956: %%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
957: %% handle_info({'EXIT',Pid,Reason}, State)
958: %% Pid = pid()
959: %% Reason = term()
960: %%
961: %% Handles exit messages from linked processes. Only test suites are
962: %% expected to be linked.  When a test suite terminates, it is removed
963: %% from the job queue.
964: 
965: handle_info(report_idle, State) ->
966:     Finish = State#state.finish,
967:     lists:foreach(fun({Cli,Fun}) -> Fun(Cli,Finish) end,
968: 		  State#state.idle_notify),
969:     {noreply,State#state{idle_notify=[]}};
970: 
971: 
972: handle_info({'EXIT',Pid,Reason}, State) ->
973:     case lists:keysearch(Pid,2,State#state.jobs) of
974: 	false ->
975: 	    %% not our problem
976: 	    {noreply,State};
977: 	{value,{Name,_}} ->
978: 	    NewJobs = lists:keydelete(Pid, 2, State#state.jobs),
979: 	    case Reason of
980: 		normal ->
981: 		    fine;
982: 		killed ->
983: 		    io:format("Suite ~ts was killed\n", [Name]);
984: 		_Other ->
985: 		    io:format("Suite ~ts was killed with reason ~tp\n",
986: 			      [Name,Reason])
987: 	    end,
988: 	    State2 = State#state{jobs=NewJobs},
989: 	    Finish = State2#state.finish,
990: 	    case NewJobs of
991: 		[] ->
992: 		    lists:foreach(fun({Cli,Fun}) -> Fun(Cli,Finish) end,
993: 				  State2#state.idle_notify),
994: 		    case Finish of
995: 			false ->
996: 			    {noreply,State2#state{idle_notify=[]}};
997: 			_ ->			% true | abort
998: 			    %% test_server:finish() has been called and
999: 			    %% there are no jobs in the job queue =>
1000: 			    %% stop the test_server_ctrl
1001: 			    {stop,shutdown,State2#state{finish=false}}
1002: 		    end;
1003: 		_ ->				% pending jobs
1004: 		    case Finish of
1005: 			abort ->		% abort test now!
1006: 			    lists:foreach(fun({Cli,Fun}) -> Fun(Cli,Finish) end,
1007: 					  State2#state.idle_notify),
1008: 			    {stop,shutdown,State2#state{finish=false}};
1009: 			_ ->			% true | false
1010: 			    {noreply, State2}
1011: 		    end
1012: 	    end
1013:     end;
1014:

1030: %% terminate(Reason, State) -> ok
1031: %% Reason = term()
1032: %%
1033: %% Cleans up when the test_server is terminating. Kills the running
1034: %% test suites (if any) and any possible remainting slave node
1035: 
1036: terminate(_Reason, State) ->
1037:     test_server_sup:util_stop(),
1038:     ok = kill_all_jobs(State#state.jobs),
1039:     _ = test_server_node:kill_nodes(),
1040:     ok.
1041: 
1042: kill_all_jobs([{_Name,JobPid}|Jobs]) ->
1043:     exit(JobPid, kill),
1044:     kill_all_jobs(Jobs);
1045: kill_all_jobs([]) ->
1046:     ok.

1053: %%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
1054: %% spawn_tester(Mod, Func, Args, Dir, Name, Levels, RejectIoReqs,
1055: %%              CreatePrivDir, TestCaseCallback, ExtraTools) -> Pid
1056: %% Mod = atom()
1057: %% Func = atom()
1058: %% Args = [term(),...]
1059: %% Dir = string()
1060: %% Name = string()
1061: %% Levels = {integer(),integer(),integer()}
1062: %% RejectIoReqs = bool()
1063: %% CreatePrivDir = auto_per_run | manual_per_tc | auto_per_tc
1064: %% TestCaseCallback = {CBMod,CBFunc} | undefined
1065: %% ExtraTools = [ExtraTool,...]
1066: %% ExtraTool = CoverInfo | TraceInfo | RandomSeed
1067: %%
1068: %% Spawns a test suite execute-process, just an ordinary spawn, except
1069: %% that it will set a lot of dictionary information before starting the
1070: %% named function. Also, the execution is timed and protected by a catch.
1071: %% When the named function is done executing, a summary of the results
1072: %% is printed to the log files.
1073: 
1074: spawn_tester(Mod, Func, Args, Dir, Name, Levels, RejectIoReqs,
1075: 	     CreatePrivDir, TCCallback, ExtraTools) ->
1076:     spawn_link(fun() ->
1077: 	      init_tester(Mod, Func, Args, Dir, Name, Levels, RejectIoReqs,
1078: 			   CreatePrivDir, TCCallback, ExtraTools)
1079:       end).
1080: 
1081: init_tester(Mod, Func, Args, Dir, Name, {_,_,MinLev}=Levels,
1082: 	    RejectIoReqs, CreatePrivDir, TCCallback, ExtraTools) ->
1083:     process_flag(trap_exit, true),
1084:     _ = test_server_io:start_link(),
1085:     put(app, common_test),
1086:     put(test_server_name, Name),
1087:     put(test_server_dir, Dir),
1088:     put(test_server_total_time, 0),
1089:     put(test_server_ok, 0),
1090:     put(test_server_failed, 0),
1091:     put(test_server_skipped, {0,0}),
1092:     put(test_server_minor_level, MinLev),
1093:     put(test_server_create_priv_dir, CreatePrivDir),
1094:     put(test_server_random_seed, proplists:get_value(random_seed, ExtraTools)),
1095:     put(test_server_testcase_callback, TCCallback),
1096:     case os:getenv("TEST_SERVER_FRAMEWORK") of
1097: 	FW when FW =:= false; FW =:= "undefined" ->
1098: 	    put(test_server_framework, '$none');	
1099: 	FW ->
1100: 	    put(test_server_framework_name, list_to_atom(FW)),
1101: 	    case os:getenv("TEST_SERVER_FRAMEWORK_NAME") of
1102: 		FWName when FWName =:= false; FWName =:= "undefined" ->
1103: 		    put(test_server_framework_name, '$none');	
1104: 		FWName ->
1105: 		    put(test_server_framework_name, list_to_atom(FWName))
1106: 	    end
1107:     end,
1108: 
1109:     %% before first print, read and set logging options
1110:     FWLogDir =
1111:         case test_server_sup:framework_call(get_log_dir, [], []) of
1112:             {ok,FwDir} -> FwDir;
1113:             _          -> filename:dirname(Dir)
1114:         end,
1115:     put(test_server_framework_logdir, FWLogDir),
1116:     LogOpts = test_server_sup:framework_call(get_logopts, [], []),
1117:     put(test_server_logopts, LogOpts),
1118: 
1119:     StartedExtraTools = start_extra_tools(ExtraTools),
1120:

1733: %%
1734: %% Create a minor log file for the test case Mod,Func,Args. The log file
1735: %% will be stored in the log directory under the name ..html.
1736: %% Some header info will also be inserted into the log file. If the test
1737: %% case runs in a parallel group, then to avoid clashing file names if the
1738: %% case is executed more than once, the name ...html
1739: %% is used.

1741: start_minor_log_file(Mod, Func, ParallelTC) ->
1742:     MFA = {Mod,Func,1},

1745:     AbsName = filename:join(LogDir, Name),

1747: 	false ->                           %% normal case, unique name
1748: 	    start_minor_log_file1(Mod, Func, LogDir, AbsName, MFA);
1749: 	true ->                            %% special case, duplicate names
1750: 	    Tag = test_server_sup:unique_name(),
1751:             Name1 = minor_log_file_name(Mod,Func,[$.|Tag]),
1752: 	    AbsName1 = filename:join(LogDir, Name1),
1753: 	    start_minor_log_file1(Mod, Func, LogDir, AbsName1, MFA)

1845: %% html_convert_modules(TestSpec, Config) -> ok
1846: %%  Isolate the modules affected by TestSpec and
1847: %%  make sure they are converted to html.
1848: %%
1849: %%  Errors are silently ignored.
1850: 
1851: html_convert_modules(TestSpec, _Config, FwMod) ->
1852:     Mods = html_isolate_modules(TestSpec, FwMod),
1853:     html_convert_modules(Mods),
1854:     copy_html_files(get(test_server_dir), get(test_server_log_dir_base)).

1856: %% Retrieve a list of modules out of the test spec.
1857: html_isolate_modules(List, FwMod) ->
1858:     html_isolate_modules(List, sets:new(), FwMod).
1859: 
1860: html_isolate_modules([], Set, _) -> sets:to_list(Set);
1861: html_isolate_modules([{skip_case,{_Case,_Cmt},_Mode}|Cases], Set, FwMod) ->
1862:     html_isolate_modules(Cases, Set, FwMod);
1863: html_isolate_modules([{conf,_Ref,Props,{FwMod,_Func}}|Cases], Set, FwMod) ->
1864:     Set1 = case proplists:get_value(suite, Props) of
1865: 	       undefined -> Set;
1866: 	       Mod -> sets:add_element(Mod, Set)
1867: 	   end,
1868:     html_isolate_modules(Cases, Set1, FwMod);
1869: html_isolate_modules([{conf,_Ref,_Props,{Mod,_Func}}|Cases], Set, FwMod) ->
1870:     html_isolate_modules(Cases, sets:add_element(Mod, Set), FwMod);
1871: html_isolate_modules([{skip_case,{conf,_Ref,{FwMod,_Func},_Cmt},Mode}|Cases],
1872: 		     Set, FwMod) ->
1873:     Set1 = case proplists:get_value(suite, get_props(Mode)) of
1874: 	       undefined -> Set;
1875: 	       Mod -> sets:add_element(Mod, Set)
1876: 	   end,
1877:     html_isolate_modules(Cases, Set1, FwMod);
1878: html_isolate_modules([{skip_case,{conf,_Ref,{Mod,_Func},_Cmt},_Props}|Cases],
1879: 		     Set, FwMod) ->
1880:     html_isolate_modules(Cases, sets:add_element(Mod, Set), FwMod);
1881: html_isolate_modules([{Mod,_Case}|Cases], Set, FwMod) ->
1882:     html_isolate_modules(Cases, sets:add_element(Mod, Set), FwMod);
1883: html_isolate_modules([{Mod,_Case,_Args}|Cases], Set, FwMod) ->
1884:     html_isolate_modules(Cases, sets:add_element(Mod, Set), FwMod).

1886: %% Given a list of modules, convert each module's source code to HTML.
1887: html_convert_modules([Mod|Mods]) ->
1888:     case code:which(Mod) of
1889: 	Path when is_list(Path) ->
1890: 	    SrcFile = filename:rootname(Path) ++ ".erl",
1891: 	    FoundSrcFile =
1892: 		case file:read_file_info(SrcFile) of
1893: 		    {ok,SInfo} ->
1894: 			{SrcFile,SInfo};
1895: 		    {error,_} ->
1896: 			ModInfo = Mod:module_info(compile),
1897: 			case proplists:get_value(source, ModInfo) of
1898: 			    undefined ->
1899: 				undefined;
1900: 			    OtherSrcFile ->
1901: 				case file:read_file_info(OtherSrcFile) of
1902: 				    {ok,SInfo} ->
1903: 					{OtherSrcFile,SInfo};
1904: 				    {error,_} ->
1905: 					undefined
1906: 				end
1907: 			end
1908: 		end,
1909: 	    case FoundSrcFile of
1910: 		undefined ->
1911: 		    html_convert_modules(Mods);
1912: 		{SrcFile1,SrcFileInfo} ->
1913: 		    DestDir = get(test_server_dir),
1914: 		    Name = atom_to_list(Mod),
1915: 		    DestFile = filename:join(DestDir,
1916: 					     downcase(Name)++?src_listing_ext),
1917: 		    _ = html_possibly_convert(SrcFile1, SrcFileInfo, DestFile),
1918: 		    html_convert_modules(Mods)
1919: 	    end;
1920: 	_Other ->
1921: 	    html_convert_modules(Mods)
1922:     end;
1923: html_convert_modules([]) -> ok.

1925: %% Convert source code to HTML if possible and needed.
1926: html_possibly_convert(Src, SrcInfo, Dest) ->
1927:     case file:read_file_info(Dest) of
1928: 	{ok,DestInfo} when DestInfo#file_info.mtime >= SrcInfo#file_info.mtime ->
1929: 	    ok;					% dest file up to date
1930: 	_ ->
1931: 	    InclPath = case application:get_env(test_server, include) of
1932: 			   {ok,Incls} -> Incls;
1933: 			   _ -> []
1934: 		       end,
1935: 
1936: 	    OutDir = get(test_server_log_dir_base),
1937: 	    case test_server_sup:framework_call(get_html_wrapper,
1938: 						["Module "++Src,false,
1939: 						 OutDir,undefined,
1940: 						 encoding(Src)], "") of
1941: 		Empty when (Empty == "") ; (element(2,Empty) == "")  ->
1942: 		    erl2html2:convert(Src, Dest, InclPath);
1943: 		{_,Header,_} ->
1944: 		    erl2html2:convert(Src, Dest, InclPath, Header)
1945: 	    end
1946:     end.

1968: add_init_and_end_per_suite([{make,_,_}=Case|Cases], LastMod, LastRef, FwMod) ->

1970: add_init_and_end_per_suite([{skip_case,{{Mod,all},_},_}=Case|Cases], LastMod,
1971: 			   LastRef, FwMod) when Mod =/= LastMod ->
1972:     {PreCases, NextMod, NextRef} =
1973: 	do_add_end_per_suite_and_skip(LastMod, LastRef, Mod, FwMod),
1974:     PreCases ++ [Case|add_init_and_end_per_suite(Cases, NextMod,
1975: 						 NextRef, FwMod)];
1976: add_init_and_end_per_suite([{skip_case,{{Mod,_},_Cmt},_Mode}=Case|Cases],
1977: 			   LastMod, LastRef, FwMod) when Mod =/= LastMod ->

1979: 	do_add_init_and_end_per_suite(LastMod, LastRef, Mod, FwMod),

1981: 						 NextRef, FwMod)];
1982: add_init_and_end_per_suite([{skip_case,{conf,_,{Mod,_},_},_}=Case|Cases],

1988: add_init_and_end_per_suite([{skip_case,{conf,_,{Mod,_},_}}=Case|Cases], LastMod,
1989: 			   LastRef, FwMod) when Mod =/= LastMod ->

1991: 	do_add_init_and_end_per_suite(LastMod, LastRef, Mod, FwMod),
1992:     PreCases ++ [Case|add_init_and_end_per_suite(Cases, NextMod,
1993: 						 NextRef, FwMod)];
1994: add_init_and_end_per_suite([{conf,Ref,Props,{FwMod,Func}}=Case|Cases], LastMod,
1995: 			   LastRef, FwMod) ->
1996:     %% if Mod == FwMod, this conf test is (probably) a test case group where
1997:     %% the init- and end-functions are missing in the suite, and if so,
1998:     %% the suite name should be stored as {suite,Suite} in Props
1999:     case proplists:get_value(suite, Props) of
2000: 	Suite when Suite =/= undefined, Suite =/= LastMod ->
2001: 	    {PreCases, NextMod, NextRef} =
2002: 		do_add_init_and_end_per_suite(LastMod, LastRef, Suite, FwMod),
2003: 	    Case1 = {conf,Ref,[{suite,NextMod}|proplists:delete(suite,Props)],
2004: 		     {FwMod,Func}},
2005: 	    PreCases ++ [Case1|add_init_and_end_per_suite(Cases, NextMod,
2006: 							  NextRef, FwMod)];
2007: 	_ ->
2008: 	    [Case|add_init_and_end_per_suite(Cases, LastMod, LastRef, FwMod)]
2009:     end;
2010: add_init_and_end_per_suite([{conf,_,_,{Mod,_}}=Case|Cases], LastMod,
2011: 			   LastRef, FwMod) when Mod =/= LastMod, Mod =/= FwMod ->
2012:     {PreCases, NextMod, NextRef} =
2013: 	do_add_init_and_end_per_suite(LastMod, LastRef, Mod, FwMod),
2014:     PreCases ++ [Case|add_init_and_end_per_suite(Cases, NextMod,
2015: 						 NextRef, FwMod)];
2016: add_init_and_end_per_suite([SkipCase|Cases], LastMod, LastRef, FwMod)
2017:   when element(1,SkipCase) == skip_case;  element(1,SkipCase) == auto_skip_case->
2018:     [SkipCase|add_init_and_end_per_suite(Cases, LastMod, LastRef, FwMod)];
2019: add_init_and_end_per_suite([{conf,_,_,_}=Case|Cases], LastMod, LastRef, FwMod) ->

2023:     {PreCases, NextMod, NextRef} =
2024: 	do_add_init_and_end_per_suite(LastMod, LastRef, Mod, FwMod),
2025:     PreCases ++ [Case|add_init_and_end_per_suite(Cases, NextMod,
2026: 						 NextRef, FwMod)];
2027: add_init_and_end_per_suite([{repeat,_,_}=Case|Cases], LastMod, LastRef, FwMod) ->

2029: add_init_and_end_per_suite([{Mod,_}=Case|Cases], LastMod, LastRef, FwMod)

2031:     {PreCases, NextMod, NextRef} =

2033:     PreCases ++ [Case|add_init_and_end_per_suite(Cases, NextMod,
2034: 						 NextRef, FwMod)];
2035: add_init_and_end_per_suite([{Mod,_,_}=Case|Cases], LastMod, LastRef, FwMod)
2036:   when Mod =/= LastMod, Mod =/= FwMod ->
2037:     {PreCases, NextMod, NextRef} =
2038: 	do_add_init_and_end_per_suite(LastMod, LastRef, Mod, FwMod),

2041: add_init_and_end_per_suite([Case|Cases], LastMod, LastRef, FwMod)->

2043: add_init_and_end_per_suite([], _LastMod, undefined, _FwMod) ->

2047: add_init_and_end_per_suite([], LastMod, LastRef, FwMod) ->
2048:     %% we'll add end_per_suite here even if it's not exported
2049:     %% (and simply let the call fail if it's missing)
2050:     case {erlang:function_exported(LastMod, end_per_suite, 1),
2051:           erlang:function_exported(LastMod, init_per_suite, 1)} of
2052: 	{false,false} ->
2053: 	    %% let's call a "fake" end_per_suite if it exists			
2054: 	    case erlang:function_exported(FwMod, end_per_suite, 1) of
2055: 		true ->					
2056: 		    [{conf,LastRef,[{suite,LastMod}],{FwMod,end_per_suite}}];
2057: 		false ->		
2058: 		    [{conf,LastRef,[],{LastMod,end_per_suite}}]
2059: 	    end;
2060: 	_ ->
2061:             %% If any of these exist, the other should too
2062:             %% (required and documented). If it isn't, it will fail
2063:             %% with reason 'undef'.
2064: 	    [{conf,LastRef,[],{LastMod,end_per_suite}}]
2065:     end.

2067: do_add_init_and_end_per_suite(LastMod, LastRef, Mod, FwMod) ->
2068:     _ = case code:is_loaded(Mod) of
2069: 	false -> code:load_file(Mod);
2070: 	_ -> ok
2071:     end,
2072:     {Init,NextMod,NextRef} =
2073: 	case {erlang:function_exported(Mod, init_per_suite, 1),
2074:               erlang:function_exported(Mod, end_per_suite, 1)} of
2075: 	    {false,false} ->
2076: 		%% let's call a "fake" init_per_suite if it exists
2077: 		case erlang:function_exported(FwMod, init_per_suite, 1) of
2078: 		    true ->
2079: 			Ref = make_ref(),
2080: 			{[{conf,Ref,[{suite,Mod}],
2081: 			   {FwMod,init_per_suite}}],Mod,Ref};
2082: 		    false ->
2083: 			{[],Mod,undefined}
2084: 		end;
2085: 	    _ ->
2086:                 %% If any of these exist, the other should too
2087:                 %% (required and documented). If it isn't, it will fail
2088:                 %% with reason 'undef'.
2089: 		Ref = make_ref(),
2090: 		{[{conf,Ref,[],{Mod,init_per_suite}}],Mod,Ref}
2091: 	end,
2092:     Cases =
2093: 	if LastRef==undefined ->
2094: 		Init;
2095: 	   LastRef==skipped_suite ->
2096: 		Init;
2097: 	   true ->
2098: 		%% we'll add end_per_suite here even if it's not exported
2099: 		%% (and simply let the call fail if it's missing)
2100: 		case {erlang:function_exported(LastMod, end_per_suite, 1),
2101:                       erlang:function_exported(LastMod, init_per_suite, 1)} of
2102: 		    {false,false} ->
2103: 			%% let's call a "fake" end_per_suite if it exists
2104: 			case erlang:function_exported(FwMod, end_per_suite, 1) of
2105: 			    true ->				
2106: 				[{conf,LastRef,[{suite,LastMod}],
2107: 				  {FwMod,end_per_suite}}|Init];
2108: 			    false ->
2109: 				[{conf,LastRef,[],{LastMod,end_per_suite}}|Init]
2110: 			end;
2111: 		    _ ->
2112:                         %% If any of these exist, the other should too
2113:                         %% (required and documented). If it isn't, it will fail
2114:                         %% with reason 'undef'.
2115: 			[{conf,LastRef,[],{LastMod,end_per_suite}}|Init]
2116:                 end
2117: 	end,
2118:     {Cases,NextMod,NextRef}.
2119: 
2120: do_add_end_per_suite_and_skip(LastMod, LastRef, Mod, FwMod) ->
2121:     case LastRef of
2122: 	No when No==undefined ; No==skipped_suite ->
2123: 	    {[],Mod,skipped_suite};
2124: 	_Ref ->

2131: 			    {[{conf,LastRef,[],{FwMod,end_per_suite}}],

2134: 			    {[{conf,LastRef,[],{LastMod,end_per_suite}}],

2138:                     %% If any of these exist, the other should too
2139:                     %% (required and documented). If it isn't, it will fail

2183: %%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
2184: %% run_test_cases_loop(TestCases, Config, TimetrapData, Mode, Status) -> ok
2185: %% TestCases = [Test,...]
2186: %% Config = [[{Key,Val},...],...]
2187: %% TimetrapData = {MultiplyTimetrap,ScaleTimetrap}
2188: %% MultiplyTimetrap = integer() | infinity
2189: %% ScaleTimetrap = bool()
2190: %% Mode = [{Ref,[Prop,..],StartTime}]
2191: %% Ref = reference()
2192: %% Prop = {name,Name} | sequence | parallel |
2193: %%        shuffle | {shuffle,Seed} |
2194: %%        repeat | {repeat,N} |
2195: %%        repeat_until_all_ok | {repeat_until_all_ok,N} |
2196: %%        repeat_until_any_ok | {repeat_until_any_ok,N} |
2197: %%        repeat_until_any_fail | {repeat_until_any_fail,N} |
2198: %%        repeat_until_all_fail | {repeat_until_all_fail,N}
2199: %% Status = [{Ref,{{Ok,Skipped,Failed},CopiedCases}}]
2200: %% Ok = Skipped = Failed = [Case,...]
2201: %%
2202: %% Execute the TestCases under configuration Config. Config is a list
2203: %% of lists, where hd(Config) holds the config tuples for the current
2204: %% conf case and tl(Config) is the data for the higher level conf cases.
2205: %% Config data is "inherited" from top to nested conf cases, but
2206: %% never the other way around. if length(Config) == 1, Config contains
2207: %% only the initial config data for the suite.
2208: %%
2209: %% Test may be one of the following:
2210: %%
2211: %% {conf,Ref,Props,{Mod,Func}} Mod:Func is a configuration modification
2212: %% function, call it with the current configuration as argument. It will
2213: %% return a new configuration.
2214: %%
2215: %% {make,Ref,{Mod,Func,Args}} Mod:Func is a make function, and it is called
2216: %% with the given arguments.
2217: %%
2218: %% {Mod,Case} This is a normal test case. Determine the correct
2219: %% configuration, and insert {Mod,Case,Config} as head of the list,
2220: %% then reiterate.
2221: %%
2222: %% {Mod,Case,Args} A test case with predefined argument (usually a normal
2223: %% test case which just got a fresh configuration (see above)).
2224: %%
2225: %% {skip_case,{conf,Ref,Case,Comment}} An init conf case gets skipped
2226: %% by the user. This will also cause the end conf case to be skipped.
2227: %% Note that it is not possible to skip an end conf case directly (it
2228: %% can only be skipped indirectly by a skipped init conf case). The
2229: %% comment (which gets printed in the log files) describes why the case
2230: %% was skipped.
2231: %%
2232: %% {skip_case,{Case,Comment},Mode} A normal test case skipped by the user.
2233: %% The comment (which gets printed in the log files) describes why the
2234: %% case was skipped.
2235: %%
2236: %% {auto_skip_case,{conf,Ref,Case,Comment},Mode} This is the result of
2237: %% an end conf case being automatically skipped due to a failing init
2238: %% conf case. It could also be a nested conf case that gets skipped
2239: %% because of a failed or skipped top level conf.
2240: %%
2241: %% {auto_skip_case,{Case,Comment},Mode} This is a normal test case which
2242: %% gets automatically skipped because of a failing init conf case or
2243: %% because of a failing previous test case in a sequence.
2244: %%
2245: %% -------------------------------------------------------------------
2246: %% Description of IO handling during execution of parallel test cases:
2247: %% -------------------------------------------------------------------
2248: %%
2249: %% A conf group can have an associated list of properties. If the
2250: %% parallel property is specified for a group, it means the test cases
2251: %% should be spawned and run in parallel rather than called sequentially
2252: %% (which is always the default mode). Test cases that execute in parallel
2253: %% also write to their respective minor log files in parallel. Printouts
2254: %% to common log files, such as the summary html file and the major log
2255: %% file on text format, still have to be processed sequentially. For this
2256: %% reason, the Mode argument specifies if a parallel group is currently
2257: %% being executed.
2258: %%
2259: %% The low-level mechanism for buffering IO for the common log files
2260: %% is handled by the test_server_io module. Buffering is turned on by
2261: %% test_server_io:start_transaction/0 and off by calling
2262: %% test_server_io:end_transaction/0. The buffered data for the transaction
2263: %% can printed by calling test_server_io:print_buffered/1.
2264: %%
2265: %% This module is responsible for turning on IO buffering and to later
2266: %% test_server_io:print_buffered/1 to print the data. To help with this,
2267: %% two variables in the process dictionary are used:
2268: %% 'test_server_common_io_handler' and 'test_server_queued_io'. The values
2269: %% are set to as following:
2270: %%
2271: %%   Value	Meaning
2272: %%   -----     -------
2273: %%   undefined	No parallel test cases running
2274: %%   {tc,Pid}	Running test cases in a top-level parallel group
2275: %%   {Ref,Pid}	Running sequential test case inside a parallel group
2276: %%
2277: %% FIXME: The Pid is no longer used.
2278: %%
2279: %% If a conf group nested under a parallel group in the test
2280: %% specification should be started, the 'test_server_common_io_handler'
2281: %% value gets set also on the main process.
2282: %%
2283: %% During execution of a parallel group (or of a group nested under a
2284: %% parallel group), *any* new test case being started gets registered
2285: %% in a list saved in the dictionary with 'test_server_queued_io' as key.
2286: %% When the top level parallel group is finished (only then can we be
2287: %% sure all parallel test cases have finished and "reported in"), the
2288: %% list of test cases is traversed in order and test_server_io:print_buffered/1
2289: %% can be called for each test case. See handle_test_case_io_and_status/0
2290: %% for details.
2291: %%
2292: %% To be able to handle nested conf groups with different properties,
2293: %% the Mode argument specifies a list of {Ref,Properties} tuples.
2294: %% The head of the Mode list at any given time identifies the group
2295: %% currently being processed. The tail of the list identifies groups
2296: %% on higher level.
2297: %%
2298: %% -------------------------------------------------------------------
2299: %% Notes on parallel execution of test cases
2300: %% -------------------------------------------------------------------
2301: %%
2302: %% A group nested under a parallel group will start executing in
2303: %% parallel with previous (parallel) test cases (no matter what
2304: %% properties the nested group has). Test cases are however never
2305: %% executed in parallel with the start or end conf case of the same
2306: %% group! Because of this, the test_server_ctrl loop waits at
2307: %% the end conf of a group for all parallel cases to finish
2308: %% before the end conf case actually executes. This has the effect
2309: %% that it's only after a nested group has finished that any
2310: %% remaining parallel cases in the previous group get spawned (*).
2311: %% Example (all parallel cases):
2312: %%
2313: %% group1_init   |---->
2314: %% group1_case1        | --------->
2315: %% group1_case2        | --------------------------------->
2316: %% group2_init         | ---->
2317: %% group2_case1               | ------>
2318: %% group2_case2               | ---------->
2319: %% group2_end                              | --->
2320: %% group1_case3                               (*)| ---->
2321: %% group1_case4                               (*)| -->
2322: %% group1_end                                              | --->
2323: %%
2324: 
2325: run_test_cases_loop([{SkipTag,CaseData={Type,_Ref,_Case,_Comment}}|Cases],
2326: 		    Config, TimetrapData, Mode, Status) when
2327:       ((SkipTag==auto_skip_case) or (SkipTag==skip_case)) and
2328:       ((Type==conf) or (Type==make)) ->
2329:     run_test_cases_loop([{SkipTag,CaseData,Mode}|Cases],
2330: 			Config, TimetrapData, Mode, Status);
2331: 
2332: run_test_cases_loop([{SkipTag,{Type,Ref,Case,Comment},SkipMode}|Cases],
2333: 		    Config, TimetrapData, Mode, Status) when
2334:       ((SkipTag==auto_skip_case) or (SkipTag==skip_case)) and
2335:       ((Type==conf) or (Type==make)) ->
2336:     ok = file:set_cwd(filename:dirname(get(test_server_dir))),
2337:     CurrIOHandler = get(test_server_common_io_handler),
2338:     ParentMode = tl(Mode),
2339: 
2340:     {AutoOrUser,ReportTag} = 
2341: 	if SkipTag == auto_skip_case -> {auto,tc_auto_skip};
2342: 	   SkipTag == skip_case      -> {user,tc_user_skip}
2343: 	end,
2344: 
2345:     %% check and update the mode for test case execution and io msg handling
2346:     case {curr_ref(Mode),check_props(parallel, Mode)} of
2347: 	{Ref,Ref} ->
2348: 	    case check_props(parallel, ParentMode) of
2349: 		false ->
2350: 		    %% this is a skipped end conf for a top level parallel
2351: 		    %% group, buffered io can be flushed
2352: 		    _ = handle_test_case_io_and_status(),
2353: 		    set_io_buffering(undefined),
2354: 		    {Mod,Func} = skip_case(AutoOrUser, Ref, 0, Case, Comment,
2355: 					   false, SkipMode),
2356: 		    ConfData = {Mod,{Func,get_name(SkipMode)},Comment},
2357: 		    test_server_sup:framework_call(report,
2358: 						   [ReportTag,ConfData]),
2359: 		    run_test_cases_loop(Cases, Config, TimetrapData, ParentMode,
2360: 					delete_status(Ref, Status));
2361: 		_ ->
2362: 		    %% this is a skipped end conf for a parallel group nested
2363: 		    %% under a parallel group (io buffering is active)
2364: 		    _ = wait_for_cases(Ref),
2365: 		    {Mod,Func} = skip_case(AutoOrUser, Ref, 0, Case, Comment,
2366: 					   true, SkipMode),
2367: 		    ConfData = {Mod,{Func,get_name(SkipMode)},Comment},
2368: 		    test_server_sup:framework_call(report, [ReportTag,ConfData]),
2369: 		    case CurrIOHandler of
2370: 			{Ref,_} ->
2371: 			    %% current_io_handler was set by start conf of this
2372: 			    %% group, so we can unset it now (no more io from main
2373: 			    %% process needs to be buffered)
2374: 			    set_io_buffering(undefined);
2375: 			_ ->
2376: 			    ok
2377: 		    end,
2378: 		    run_test_cases_loop(Cases, Config,
2379: 					TimetrapData, ParentMode,
2380: 					delete_status(Ref, Status))
2381: 	    end;
2382: 	{Ref,false} ->
2383: 	    %% this is a skipped end conf for a non-parallel group that's not
2384: 	    %% nested under a parallel group
2385: 	    {Mod,Func} = skip_case(AutoOrUser, Ref, 0, Case, Comment,
2386: 				   false, SkipMode),
2387: 	    ConfData = {Mod,{Func,get_name(SkipMode)},Comment},
2388: 	    test_server_sup:framework_call(report, [ReportTag,ConfData]),
2389: 
2390: 	    %% Check if this group is auto skipped because of error in the
2391: 	    %% init conf. If so, check if the parent group is a sequence,
2392: 	    %% and if it is, skip all proceeding tests in that group.
2393: 	    GrName = get_name(Mode),
2394: 	    Cases1 =
2395: 		case get_tc_results(Status) of
2396: 		    {_,_,Fails} when length(Fails) > 0 ->
2397: 			case lists:member({group_result,GrName}, Fails) of
2398: 			    true ->
2399: 				case check_prop(sequence, ParentMode) of
2400: 				    false ->
2401: 					Cases;
2402: 				    ParentRef ->
2403: 					Reason = {group_result,GrName,failed},
2404: 					skip_cases_upto(ParentRef, Cases,
2405: 							Reason, tc, ParentMode,
2406: 							SkipTag)
2407: 				end;
2408: 			    false ->
2409: 				Cases
2410: 			end;
2411: 		    _ ->
2412: 			Cases
2413: 		end,
2414: 	    run_test_cases_loop(Cases1, Config, TimetrapData, ParentMode,
2415: 				delete_status(Ref, Status));
2416: 	{Ref,_} ->
2417: 	    %% this is a skipped end conf for a non-parallel group nested under
2418: 	    %% a parallel group (io buffering is active)
2419: 	    {Mod,Func} = skip_case(AutoOrUser, Ref, 0, Case, Comment,
2420: 				   true, SkipMode),
2421: 	    ConfData = {Mod,{Func,get_name(SkipMode)},Comment},
2422: 	    test_server_sup:framework_call(report, [ReportTag,ConfData]),
2423: 	    case CurrIOHandler of
2424: 		{Ref,_} ->
2425: 		    %% current_io_handler was set by start conf of this
2426: 		    %% group, so we can unset it now (no more io from main
2427: 		    %% process needs to be buffered)
2428: 		    set_io_buffering(undefined);
2429: 		_ ->
2430: 		    ok
2431: 	    end,
2432: 	    run_test_cases_loop(Cases, Config, TimetrapData, tl(Mode),
2433: 				delete_status(Ref, Status));
2434: 	{_,false} ->
2435: 	    %% this is a skipped start conf for a group which is not nested
2436: 	    %% under a parallel group
2437: 	    {Mod,Func} = skip_case(AutoOrUser, Ref, 0, Case, Comment,
2438: 				   false, SkipMode),
2439: 	    ConfData = {Mod,{Func,get_name(SkipMode)},Comment},
2440: 	    test_server_sup:framework_call(report, [ReportTag,ConfData]),
2441: 	    run_test_cases_loop(Cases, Config, TimetrapData,
2442: 				[conf(Ref,[])|Mode], Status);
2443: 	{_,Ref0} when is_reference(Ref0) ->
2444: 	    %% this is a skipped start conf for a group nested under a parallel
2445: 	    %% group and if this is the first nested group, io buffering must
2446: 	    %% be activated
2447: 	    if CurrIOHandler == undefined ->
2448: 		    set_io_buffering({Ref,self()});
2449: 	       true ->
2450: 		    ok
2451: 	    end,
2452: 	    {Mod,Func} = skip_case(AutoOrUser, Ref, 0, Case, Comment,
2453: 				   true, SkipMode),
2454: 	    ConfData = {Mod,{Func,get_name(SkipMode)},Comment},
2455: 	    test_server_sup:framework_call(report, [ReportTag,ConfData]),
2456: 	    run_test_cases_loop(Cases, Config, TimetrapData,
2457: 				[conf(Ref,[])|Mode], Status)
2458:     end;
2459: 
2460: run_test_cases_loop([{auto_skip_case,{Case,Comment},SkipMode}|Cases],
2461: 		    Config, TimetrapData, Mode, Status) ->
2462:     {Mod,Func} = skip_case(auto, undefined, get(test_server_case_num)+1,
2463: 			   Case, Comment, is_io_buffered(), SkipMode),
2464:     test_server_sup:framework_call(report, [tc_auto_skip,
2465: 					    {Mod,{Func,get_name(SkipMode)},
2466: 					     Comment}]),
2467:     run_test_cases_loop(Cases, Config, TimetrapData, Mode,
2468: 			update_status(skipped, Mod, Func, Status));
2469: 
2470: run_test_cases_loop([{skip_case,{{Mod,all}=Case,Comment},SkipMode}|Cases],
2471: 		    Config, TimetrapData, Mode, Status) ->
2472:     _ = skip_case(user, undefined, 0, Case, Comment, false, SkipMode),
2473:     test_server_sup:framework_call(report, [tc_user_skip,
2474: 					    {Mod,{all,get_name(SkipMode)},
2475: 					     Comment}]),
2476:     run_test_cases_loop(Cases, Config, TimetrapData, Mode, Status);
2477: 
2478: run_test_cases_loop([{skip_case,{Case,Comment},SkipMode}|Cases],
2479: 		    Config, TimetrapData, Mode, Status) ->
2480:     {Mod,Func} = skip_case(user, undefined, get(test_server_case_num)+1,
2481: 			   Case, Comment, is_io_buffered(), SkipMode),
2482:     test_server_sup:framework_call(report, [tc_user_skip,
2483: 					    {Mod,{Func,get_name(SkipMode)},
2484: 					     Comment}]),
2485:     run_test_cases_loop(Cases, Config, TimetrapData, Mode,
2486: 			update_status(skipped, Mod, Func, Status));
2487: 
2488: %% a start *or* end conf case, wrapping test cases or other conf cases
2489: run_test_cases_loop([{conf,Ref,Props,{Mod,Func}}|_Cases]=Cs0,
2490: 		    Config, TimetrapData, Mode0, Status) ->
2491:     CurrIOHandler = get(test_server_common_io_handler),
2492:     %% check and update the mode for test case execution and io msg handling
2493:     {StartConf,Mode,IOHandler,ConfTime,Status1} =
2494: 	case {curr_ref(Mode0),check_props(parallel, Mode0)} of
2495: 	    {Ref,Ref} ->
2496: 		case check_props(parallel, tl(Mode0)) of
2497: 		    false ->
2498: 			%% this is an end conf for a top level parallel group,
2499: 			%% collect results from the test case processes
2500: 			%% and calc total time
2501: 			OkSkipFail = handle_test_case_io_and_status(),
2502: 			ok = file:set_cwd(filename:dirname(get(test_server_dir))),
2503: 			After = ?now,
2504: 			Before = get(test_server_parallel_start_time),
2505: 			Elapsed = timer:now_diff(After, Before)/1000000,
2506: 			put(test_server_total_time, Elapsed),
2507: 			{false,tl(Mode0),undefined,Elapsed,
2508: 			 update_status(Ref, OkSkipFail, Status)};
2509: 		    _ ->
2510: 			%% this is an end conf for a parallel group nested under a
2511: 			%% parallel group (io buffering is active)
2512: 			OkSkipFail = wait_for_cases(Ref),
2513: 			queue_test_case_io(Ref, self(), 0, Mod, Func),

-module(cte_track).
-moduledoc false.
%% module for tracking CT execution progress
%% test spec addition examples:
%% {event_handler, {cte_track, []}}.
%% {event_handler, {cte_track, [{file, "/tmp/log.txt"}]}}.

-behaviour(gen_event).

%% gen_event callbacks
-export([init/1, handle_event/2, handle_call/2,
	 handle_info/2, terminate/2, code_change/3]).
-include("ct_event.hrl").

%%====================================================================
%% gen_event callbacks
%%====================================================================
init(InitArgs) ->
    Device =
        case proplists:get_value(file, InitArgs) of
            undefined ->
                user;
            Path when is_list(Path) ->
                {ok, D} = file:open(Path, [write]),
                D
        end,
    [begin
         dbg:start(),
         dbg:tracer(),
         dbg:tp(?MODULE, handle_event, 2, []),
         dbg:p(all,c),
         print(Device, "DEBUG started ~n")
     end || lists:member(debug, InitArgs)],
    {ok, #{device => Device,
           suite => undefined, group => undefined,
           test_stats => {0, 0, {0, 0}},
           test => #{ok => [], skipped => [], failed => [], auto_skipped => []},
           conf => #{ok => [], skipped => [], failed => [], auto_skipped => []},
           start_time => get_seconds()}}.

handle_event(#event{name = test_stats, data = TestStats}, State) ->
    {ok, maps:put(test_stats, TestStats, State)};
handle_event(#event{name = tc_start,
                    data = {Suite, init_per_suite}},
             State0 = #{device := D,
                       test_stats := TestStats}) ->
    print(D, "~n~p: ", [Suite]),
    State1 = maps:put(suite, Suite, State0),
    State = maps:put(suite_stats0, TestStats, State1),
    {ok, State};
handle_event(#event{name = tc_start,
                    data = {_Suite, {init_per_group, GroupName, _}}},
             State) ->
    {ok, maps:put(group, GroupName, State)};
handle_event(#event{name = Name,
                    data = {Suite, end_per_suite, Result}},
             State0 = #{device := Device, group := Group,
                        suite_stats0 := {SOk, SFailed, {SUserSkip, SAutoSkip}},
                        test_stats := {Ok, Failed, {UserSkip, AutoSkip}}})
  when Name == tc_done; Name == tc_user_skip; Name == tc_auto_skip->
    State1 = maps:put(suite, undefined, State0),
    State2 = maps:put(group, undefined, State1),
    State =
        case Name of
            tc_done ->
                handle_result(Suite, Group, end_per_suite, Result, undefined,
                              State2);
            Skip when Skip == tc_user_skip; Skip == tc_auto_skip ->
                handle_result(Suite, Group, end_per_suite, skipped, Result,
                              State2)
        end,
    print(Device, " | ~p ok, ~p failed, ~pU/~pA skipped",
          [Ok - SOk, Failed - SFailed, UserSkip - SUserSkip, AutoSkip - SAutoSkip]),
    {ok, State};
handle_event(#event{name = tc_done,
                    data = {Suite, Case, ok}},
             State = #{group := Group})
  when is_atom(Case) ->
    {ok, handle_result(Suite, Group, Case, ok, undefined, State)};
handle_event(#event{name = tc_done,
                    data = {_Suite, Case, {SkipOrFailed, Reason}}},
             State = #{suite := Suite, group := Group})
  when is_atom(Case) ->
    {ok, handle_result(Suite, Group, Case, SkipOrFailed, Reason, State)};
handle_event(#event{name = tc_done,
                    data = {_Suite, {Case, _, _}, {skipped, Reason}}},
             State = #{suite := Suite, group := Group})
  when Case == init_per_group; Case == end_per_group ->
    {ok, handle_result(Suite, Group, Case, skipped, Reason, State)};
handle_event(#event{name = tc_done,
                    data = {_Suite, {Case, _, _}, ok}},
             State)
  when Case == init_per_group; Case == end_per_group->
    % FIXME - not storing conf function result
    {ok, State};
handle_event(#event{name = tc_done,
                    data = Data},
             State = #{device := D}) ->
    print(D, "~n~n[cte_track] Unhandled interesting event:~nName = tc_done~nData = ~p~n~n",
          [Data]),
    {ok, State};
handle_event(#event{name = Name, data = {Suite, {Case, Group}, Comment}},
             State) when Name == tc_user_skip; Name == tc_auto_skip ->
    {ok, handle_result(Suite, Group, Case, skipped, Comment, State)};
handle_event(#event{name = Name, data = {Suite, Case, Comment}},
             State) when Name == tc_user_skip; Name == tc_auto_skip ->
    {ok, handle_result(Suite, undefined, Case, skipped, Comment, State)};
handle_event(#event{name = test_done},
             State = #{test := Test,
                       conf := Conf,
                       start_time := StartTime,
                       device := D,
                       test_stats := {Ok, Failed, {UserSkip, AutoSkip}}}) ->
    print_line(D),
    PrintCategory =
        fun(Result, Results) ->
                List = maps:get(Result, Results),
                [begin
                     print_entry(D, Result, I)
                 end || I <- lists:reverse(List)]
        end,
    print(D, "# CONF SUMMARY~n"),
    PrintCategory(auto_skipped, Conf),
    PrintCategory(failed, Conf),
    print(D, "# TEST SUMMARY~n"),
    PrintCategory(auto_skipped, Test),
    PrintCategory(failed, Test),
    print(D, "~n"),
    GetCount = fun(Result) ->
                   length(maps:get(Result, Conf))
               end,
    print(D,
          "# CONF TOTALS ~p ok, ~p failed, ~pU/~pA skipped~n" ++
          "# TEST TOTALS ~p ok, ~p failed, ~pU/~pA skipped~n" ++
              "# TIME ELAPSED ~s~n",
          [GetCount(ok), GetCount(failed), GetCount(skipped),
           GetCount(auto_skipped)] ++
          [Ok, Failed, UserSkip, AutoSkip,
           get_nice_time(get_seconds() - StartTime)]),
    print_line(D),
    print(D, "~n"),
    {ok,State};
handle_event(#event{name = Name, data = Data}, State = #{device := D}) ->
    NotInteresting = [start_logging, start_write_file, finished_write_file,
                      test_stats, start_make, finished_make, tc_logfile,
                      test_start, start_info, tc_start, stop_logging,
                      benchmark_data],
    case lists:member(Name, NotInteresting) of
        false ->
            print(D, "~n~n[cte_track] Unhandled interesting event:~nName = ~p~nData = ~p~n~n",
                  [Name, Data]);
        _ ->
            ok
    end,
    {ok,State}.

handle_call(_Req, State) ->
    Reply = ok,
    {ok, Reply, State}.

handle_info(_Info, State) ->
    {ok, State}.

terminate(stop, #{device := user}) ->
    ok;
terminate(stop, #{device := Device}) ->
    file:close(Device),
    ok;
terminate(Reason, #{device := D}) ->
    print(D, "~n[cte_track]  > Interesting terminate reason = ~p~n", [Reason]),
    ok.

code_change(_OldVsn, State, _Extra) ->
    {ok, State}.

%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
print(Device, Fmt) ->
    print(Device, Fmt, []).

print(Device, Fmt, Args) ->
    io:fwrite(Device, Fmt, Args).

print_line(Device) ->
    print(Device, "~n======================================================================~n").

% FIXME - split handle_result into: store_event and present_event
handle_result(Suite, _Group, all, skipped, _Reason,
              State0 = #{device := Device}) ->
    % FIXME store this conf fun result
    print(Device, "~n~p: suite skipped", [Suite]),
    State0;
handle_result(Suite, Group, Case, Result, Reason0,
              State0 = #{device := Device}) ->
    Type = type(Case),
    TypeResults = maps:get(Type, State0),
    TypeResultAcc = maps:get(Result, TypeResults, []),
    Reason =
        case lists:keyfind(Reason0, 4, TypeResultAcc) of
            false ->
                Reason0;
            _ ->
                saved
        end,
    Entry = {Suite, Group, Case, Reason},
    [print_entry(Device, Result, Entry) ||
        is_test(Case)],
    maps:put(Type,
             maps:put(Result, [Entry | TypeResultAcc], TypeResults),
             State0).

print_entry(Device, Result, _Entry) when Result == ok; Result == skipped ->
    print(Device, "~s", [result_short(Result)]);
print_entry(Device, Result, Entry) when is_atom(Result) ->
    print_entry(Device, result_long(Result), Entry);
print_entry(Device, Result, {Suite, undefined, Case, Reason}) ->
    print(Device, "~n~s ~p:~p ~s~n",
          [Result, Suite, Case, format_reason(Reason)]);
print_entry(Device, Result, {Suite, Group, Case, Reason}) ->
    print(Device, "~n~s ~p@~p:~p ~s~n",
          [Result, Suite, Group, Case, format_reason(Reason)]).

%result_short(failed) -> "F";
result_short(ok) -> ".";
result_short(R) when R == skipped; R == auto_skipped -> "S";
result_short(_R) -> "?".

result_long(R) when R == skipped; R == auto_skipped; R == ok; R == failed ->
    io_lib:format("[~s]", [atom_to_list(R)]);
result_long(_) -> "[?]".

format_reason(saved) ->
    "";
format_reason(Reason) when is_atom(Reason) ->
    io_lib:format("Reason: ~p", [Reason]);
format_reason(Reason) when is_list(Reason) ->
    io_lib:format("Reason: ~p", [lists:flatten(Reason)]);
format_reason({Reason, SubReason}) ->
    io_lib:format("Reason: ~p (~p)", [Reason, SubReason]);
format_reason({Reason, A, B, C}) ->
    io_lib:format("Reason: ~p (~p ~p ~p)", [Reason, A, B, C]);
format_reason(undefined) ->
    "";
format_reason(Reason) ->
    io_lib:format("~n > Not recognized reason FIXME! ~p", [Reason]).

get_nice_time(Seconds) when is_integer(Seconds) ->
    case Seconds < 60 of
        true ->
            io_lib:format("~ws", [Seconds]);
        _ ->
            io_lib:format("~wm", [round(Seconds/60)])
    end.

get_seconds() ->
    erlang:system_time(second).

%% get_stats(#{ok := Ok, skipped := Skipped, auto_skipped := AutoSkipped,
%%             failed := Failed}) ->
%%     OkLength = length(Ok),
%%     SkippedLength = length(Skipped) + length(AutoSkipped),
%%     FailedLength = length(Failed),
%%     Total = OkLength + SkippedLength + FailedLength,
%%     [OkLength, SkippedLength, FailedLength, Total].

type(Case) ->
    case is_test(Case) of
        true -> test;
        _ -> conf
    end.

is_test(Case) ->
    not is_config(Case).

is_config(Case) ->
    % FIXME add 'all'?
    lists:member(Case, [init_per_suite, end_per_suite,
                        init_per_group, end_per_group,
                        init_per_testcase, end_per_testcase]).

Done. I added Common Test progress tracking (matching the upstream `cte_track` design) plus a small correctness fix it depends on.

**New module** — `lib/common_test/src/cte_track.erl`
A `gen_event` handler you attach as a CT event handler. It tracks the run via `tc_start`/`tc_done`/`tc_user_skip`/`tc_auto_skip`/`test_stats` events and:
- prints **live progress** per suite (`.` = ok, `S` = skip) and prints each **failure immediately** as it happens, e.g. `[failed] my_SUITE@grp:tc Reason: ...`;
- prints a **readable summary when the run ends** (`test_done`): `# CONF SUMMARY`, `# TEST SUMMARY` (failed + auto-skipped cases with reasons), `# TEST TOTALS n ok, n failed, nU/nA skipped`, and `# TIME ELAPSED` — compact enough to scan in a GitHub Actions log;
- can **log everything to a file** instead of stdout via `{file, "/path/progress.log"}`.

Usage:
- Test spec: `{event_handler, {cte_track, []}}.` or `{event_handler, {cte_track, [{file, "/tmp/ct.log"}]}}.`
- API: `ct:run_test([{event_handler,{cte_track,[]}}, ...]).`

**Supporting change** — `lib/common_test/src/ct_framework.erl:764`
Test cases that return `{fail,Reason}` were normalized to `ok` before reaching `end_tc`, so `tc_done` events (and hence the tracker's failure list) missed the most common CT failure form. `tc_result/3` reintroduces the failure for plain test cases so events and the summary stay accurate. Crash/throw/`exit` paths already reported correctly and are unchanged (verified against the existing `ct_event_handler_SUITE` contract: `exit('Failing')` → `{failed,{error,'Failing'}}`).

Compiles clean under `-Werror`.

The Erlang code server currently has a fallback mechanism in `mod_to_bin/3` where, if the module cannot be found in any of the code paths, it tries a final lookup using `erl_prim_loader:get_file/1`. This fallback is problematic because it can find modules from paths that were not explicitly added via `-pa`, `-pz`, or `code:add_path*`, which makes it impossible to effectively remove such paths once they are added — the module lookup still succeeds via this implicit path.

    The goal is to remove this fallback so that module lookup strictly depends only on the paths that the user has explicitly configured. This will make code path management predictable and deterministic: if a path is removed, modules from that path will no longer be loadable.

    Note that this fallback should be removed only in the non-embedded code server path. The embedded mode does not use this fallback anyway. Also, ensure that any use of `erl_prim_loader:get_file/1` for actual file loading (not module lookup) remains unaffected.

25: Process Tracing Profiling Tool
26: 
27: `tprof` provides convenience helpers for Erlang process profiling. Underlying
28: mechanism is the Erlang trace BIFs.
29: 
30: > #### Warning {: .warning }
31: >
32: > This module aims to replace `eprof` and `cprof` into a unified API for
33: > measuring call count, time, and allocation. It is experimental in Erlang/OTP
34: > 27.0.
35: 
36: It is possible to analyze the number of calls, the time spent by function, and
37: heap allocations by function. Profiling can be done ad-hoc or run in a
38: server-aided mode for deeper introspection of the code running in production.
39: 
40: > #### Warning {: .warning }
41: >
42: > Avoid hot code reload for modules that are participating in the tracing.
43: > Reloading a module turns tracing off, discarding accumulated statistics.
44: > `tprof` may not report correct amounts when code reload happened during
45: > profiling session.
46: 
47: The `type` option controls which type of profiling to perform. You can choose
48: between `call_count`, `call_time`, and `call_memory`. The default is
49: `call_count`, it has the smallest footprint on the system but it does not
50: support per-process profiling. For this reason, all of the examples below use
51: `call_memory`, which measures heap allocation, and provide a more complex
52: feature set to demonstrate.
53: 
54: Heap allocations happen for all Erlang terms that do not fit a single machine
55: word. For example, a function returning tuple of 2 elements needs to allocate
56: this tuple on the process heap. Actual consumption is more than 2 machine words,
57: because Erlang runtime needs to store tuple size and other internal information.
58: 
59: > #### Note {: .info }
60: >
61: > When profiling is enabled, expect a slowdown in the program execution.
62: >
63: > For profiling convenience, measurements are accumulated for functions that are
64: > not enabled in trace pattern. Consider this call stack example:
65: >
66: > ```text
67: >       top_traced_function(...)
68: >       not_traced_function()
69: >       bottom_traced_function()
70: > ```
71: >
72: > Allocations that happened within `not_traced_function` will be accounted into
73: > `top_traced_function`. However allocations happened within
74: > `bottom_traced_function` are not included in the `top_traced_function`. If you
75: > want to account only own allocations, you need to trace all functions.
76: 
77: ## Ad-hoc profiling
78: 
79: Basic profiling providing accumulated memory allocation data. You can choose to
80: print per-process statistics, total statistics, or omit printing and extract
81: machine-readable data that you can later sort/print:
82: 
83: ```text
84:       1> tprof:profile(lists, seq, [1, 16], #{type => call_memory}).
85: 
86:       ****** Process <0.179.0>    -- 100.00 % of total allocations ***
87:       FUNCTION          CALLS  WORDS  PER CALL  [     %]
88:       lists:seq_loop/3      5     32         6  [100.00]
89:       32            [ 100.0]
90:       ok
91: ```

117: 
118: Ad-hoc profiling results may be printed in a few different ways. Following
119: examples are using `test` module defined like this:
120: 
121: ```erlang
122:       -module(test).
123:       -export([test_spawn/0]).
124:       test_spawn() ->
125:           {Pid, MRef} = spawn_monitor(fun () -> lists:seq(1, 32) end),
126:           receive
127:               {'DOWN', MRef, process, Pid, normal} ->
128:                   done
129:           end.
130: ```
131: 
132: Default format prints per-process statistics.
133: 
134: ```text
135:         2> tprof:profile(test, test_spawn, [], #{type => call_memory}).
136: 
137:         ****** Process <0.176.0>    -- 23.66 % of total allocations ***
138:         FUNCTION                CALLS  WORDS  PER CALL  [    %]
139:         erlang:spawn_monitor/1      1      2         2  [ 9.09]
140:         erlang:spawn_opt/4          1      6         6  [27.27]
141:         test:test_spawn/0           1     14        14  [63.64]
142:                                           22            [100.0]
143: 
144:         ****** Process <0.177.0>    -- 76.34 % of total allocations ***
145:         FUNCTION           CALLS  WORDS  PER CALL  [    %]
146:         erlang:apply/2         1      7         7  [ 9.86]
147:         lists:seq_loop/3       9     64         7  [90.14]
148:                                      71            [100.0]
149: ```
150: 
151: This example prints the combined memory allocation of all processes, sorted by
152: total allocated words in the descending order
153: 
154: ```erlang
155:         5> tprof:profile(test, test_spawn, [],
156:                          #{type => call_memory, report => {total, {words, descending}}}).
157: 
158:         FUNCTION                CALLS  WORDS  PER CALL  [    %]
159:         lists:seq_loop/3            9     64         7  [68.82]
160:         test:test_spawn/0           1     14        14  [15.05]
161:         erlang:apply/2              1      7         7  [ 7.53]
162:         erlang:spawn_opt/4          1      6         6  [ 6.45]
163:         erlang:spawn_monitor/1      1      2         2  [ 2.15]
164:                                           93            [100.0]
165: ```
166: 
167: You can also collect the profile for further inspection.
168: 
169: ```erlang
170:       6> {done, ProfileData} = tprof:profile(fun test:test_spawn/0,
171:                                              #{type => call_memory, report => return}).
172:       <...>
173:       7> tprof:format(tprof:inspect(ProfileData, process, {percent, descending})).
174: 
175:       ****** Process <0.223.0>    -- 23.66 % of total allocations ***
176:       FUNCTION                CALLS  WORDS  PER CALL  [    %]
177:       test:test_spawn/0           1     14        14  [63.64]
178:       erlang:spawn_opt/4          1      6         6  [27.27]
179:       erlang:spawn_monitor/1      1      2         2  [ 9.09]
180:       22            [100.0]
181: 
182:       ****** Process <0.224.0>    -- 76.34 % of total allocations ***
183:       FUNCTION           CALLS  WORDS  PER CALL  [    %]
184:       lists:seq_loop/3       9     64         7  [90.14]
185:       erlang:apply/2         1      7         7  [ 9.86]
186:       71            [100.0]
187: ```
188: 
189: The processes which are profiled depends on the profiling type. `call_count`,
190: the default, will count calls across all processes. The other types, `call_time`
191: and `call_memory`, take into account all processes spawned from the
192: user-provided function (using `set_on_spawn` argument for trace/3 BIF). You
193: cannot restrict the profiled processes for `call_count`, but you can limit the
194: trace to a single process for the other two:
195: 
196: ```text
197:       2> tprof:profile(test, test_spawn, [],
198:                        #{type => call_memory, set_on_spawn => false}).
199: 
200:       ****** Process <0.183.0>    -- 100.00 % of total allocations ***
201:       FUNCTION                CALLS  WORDS  PER CALL  [    %]
202:       erlang:spawn_monitor/1      1      2         2  [ 9.09]
203:       erlang:spawn_opt/4          1      6         6  [27.27]
204:       test:test_spawn/0           1     14        14  [63.64]
205: ```
206: 
207: [](){: #pg_example }
208: 
209: Erlang programs may perform expensive operations in processes that are different
210: from the original one. You can include multiple, new or even all processes in
211: the trace when measuring time or memory:
212: 
213: ```text
214:       7> pg:start_link().
215:       {ok,<0.252.0>}
216:       8> tprof:profile(fun() -> pg:join(group, self()) end,
217:                        #{type => call_memory, rootset => [pg]}).
218:       ****** Process <0.252.0>    -- 52.86 % of total allocations ***
219:       FUNCTION                      CALLS  WORDS  PER CALL  [    %]
220:       pg:leave_local_update_ets/5       1      2         2  [ 1.80]
221:       gen:reply/2                       1      3         3  [ 2.70]
222:       erlang:monitor/2                  1      3         3  [ 2.70]
223:       gen_server:try_handle_call/4      1      3         3  [ 2.70]
224:       gen_server:try_dispatch/4         1      3         3  [ 2.70]
225:       maps:iterator/1                   2      4         2  [ 3.60]
226:       maps:take/2                       1      6         6  [ 5.41]
227:       pg:join_local_update_ets/5        1      8         8  [ 7.21]
228:       pg:handle_info/2                  1      8         8  [ 7.21]
229:       pg:handle_call/3                  1      9         9  [ 8.11]
230:       gen_server:loop/7                 2      9         4  [ 8.11]
231:       ets:lookup/2                      2     10         5  [ 9.01]
232:       pg:join_local/3                   1     11        11  [ 9.91]
233:       pg:notify_group/5                 2     16         8  [14.41]
234:       erlang:setelement/3               2     16         8  [14.41]
235:       111            [100.0]
236: 
237:       ****** Process <0.255.0>    -- 47.14 % of total allocations ***
238:       FUNCTION                   CALLS  WORDS  PER CALL  [    %]
239:       erl_eval:match_list/6          1      3         3  [ 3.03]
240:       erlang:monitor/2               1      3         3  [ 3.03]
241:       lists:reverse/1                2      4         2  [ 4.04]
242:       pg:join/3                      1      4         4  [ 4.04]
243:       erl_eval:add_bindings/2        1      5         5  [ 5.05]
244:       erl_eval:do_apply/7            2      6         3  [ 6.06]
245:       gen:call/4                     1      8         8  [ 8.08]
246:       erl_eval:expr_list/7           4     10         2  [10.10]
247:       gen:do_call/4                  1     16        16  [16.16]
248:       erl_eval:ret_expr/3            4     16         4  [16.16]
249:       erl_eval:merge_bindings/4      3     24         8  [24.24]
250:       99            [100.0]
251: ```
252: 
253: There is no default limit on the profiling time. It is possible to define such
254: limit for ad-hoc profile. If function being profiled does not return in a
255: specified amount of time, process is terminated with `kill` reason. Any unlinked
256: children started by the user-supplied function are kept, it is developer's
257: responsibility to ensure cleanup.
258: 
259: ```erlang
260:       9> tprof:profile(timer, sleep, [100000], #{timeout => 1000}).
261: ```
262: 
263: By default, only one ad-hoc or server-aided profiling session is allowed at any
264: point in time. It is possible to force multiple ad-hoc sessions concurrently,
265: but it is developer responsibility to ensure non-overlapping trace patterns.
266: 
267: ```erlang
268:       1> tprof:profile(fun() -> lists:seq(1, 32) end,
269:           #{registered => false, pattern => [{lists, '_', '_'}]}).
270: ```
271: 
272: ## Server-aided profiling
273: 
274: Memory profiling can be done when your system is up and running. You can start
275: the `tprof` server, add trace patterns and processes to trace while your system
276: handles actual traffic. You can extract the data any time, inspect, and print.
277: The example below traces activity of all processes supervised by kernel:
278: 
279: ```erlang
280:       1> tprof:start(#{type => call_memory}).
281:       {ok,<0.200.0>}
282:       2> tprof:enable_trace({all_children, kernel_sup}).
283:       34
284:       3> tprof:set_pattern('_', '_' , '_').
285:       16728
286:       4> Sample = tprof:collect().
287:       [{gen_server,try_dispatch,4,[{<0.154.0>,2,6}]},
288:       {erlang,iolist_to_iovec,1,[{<0.161.0>,1,8}]},
289:       <...>
290:       5 > tprof:format(tprof:inspect(Sample)).
291: 
292:       ****** Process <0.154.0>    -- 14.21 % of total allocations ***
293:       FUNCTION                   CALLS  WORDS  PER CALL  [    %]
294:       maps:iterator/1                2      4         2  [15.38]
295:       gen_server:try_dispatch/4      2      6         3  [23.08]
296:       net_kernel:handle_info/2       2     16         8  [61.54]
297:                                            26            [100.0]
298: 
299:       ****** Process <0.161.0>    -- 85.79 % of total allocations ***
300:       FUNCTION                        CALLS  WORDS  PER CALL  [    %]
301:       disk_log:handle/2                   2      2         1  [ 1.27]
302:       disk_log_1:maybe_start_timer/1      1      3         3  [ 1.91]
303:       disk_log_1:mf_write_cache/1         1      3         3  [ 1.91]
304:       <...>
305: ```
306: 
307: [](){: #inspect_example }
308: 
309: It is possible to profile the entire running system, and then examine individual
310: processes:
311: 
312: ```erlang
313:       1> tprof:start(#{type => call_memory}).
314:       2> tprof:enable_trace(processes), tprof:set_pattern('_', '_' , '_').
315:       9041
316:       3> timer:sleep(10000), tprof:disable_trace(processes), Sample = tprof:collect().
317:       [{user_drv,server,3,[{<0.64.0>,12,136}]},
318:       {user_drv,contains_ctrl_g_or_ctrl_c,1,[{<0.64.0>,80,10}]},
319:       <...>
320:       4> Inspected = tprof:inspect(Sample, process, words), Shell = maps:get(self(), Inspected).
321:       {2743,
322:       [{shell,{enc,0},1,2,2,0.07291286912139992},
323:       <...>
324:       5> tprof:format(Shell).
325: 
326:       FUNCTION                           CALLS  WORDS  PER CALL  [    %]
327:       <...>
328:       erl_lint:start/2                       2    300       150  [10.94]
329:       shell:used_records/1                 114    342         3  [12.47]
330: ```
331: """.

549: The same as
550: [`enable_trace` ](`enable_trace/2`)`(Spec, #{set_on_spawn => true})`.

553: -spec enable_trace(Spec) -> non_neg_integer()
554:     when Spec :: pid() |
555:         processes |
556:         new_processes |
557:         existing_processes |
558:         {children | all_children, process()};
559:     ([process()]) -> non_neg_integer() | {non_neg_integer(), [process()]}.

563: -doc """
564: Similar to `erlang:trace/3`, but supports a few more options for tracing
565: convenience. Tracing per process is not supported by `call_count` profilers.
566: 
567: `Spec` is either a process identifier (pid) for a local process, one of the
568: following atoms, or a list of local process identifiers or their registered
569: names:
570: 
571: - **`processes`** - All currently existing processes and all that will be
572:   created in the future.
573: 
574: - **`existing_processes`** - All currently existing processes.
575: 
576: - **`new_processes`** - All processes that will be created in the future.
577: 
578: - **`children`** - All currently running processes that were directly spawned by
579:   the specified process. This mode is helpful for tracing workers of a single
580:   supervisor.
581: 
582: - **`all_children`** - All currently running processes that were spawned by the
583:   specified process, or any recursive descendant of it. This mode is designed to
584:   facilitate tracing of supervision trees.
585: 
586: > #### Note {: .info }
587: >
588: > The profiling server does not keep track of processes that were added to the
589: > tracing set. It is permitted to stop the profiling server (wiping out any
590: > accumulated data), restart the server, set entirely different tracing pattern
591: > keeping the list of traced processes for future use. Use
592: > [`disable_trace`(processes)](`disable_trace/2`) to clear the list of traced
593: > processes.
594: 
595: Specify `Options` to modify tracing behaviour:
596: 
597: - **`set_on_spawn`** - Automatically start tracing for processes spawned by the
598:   traced process. On by default.
599: """.
600: -doc(#{since => <<"OTP @OTP-18756@">>}).
601: -spec enable_trace(Spec, trace_options()) -> non_neg_integer()
602:     when Spec :: pid() |
603:         processes |
604:         new_processes |
605:         existing_processes |
606:         {children | all_children, process()};
607:     ([process()], trace_options()) -> non_neg_integer() | {non_neg_integer(), [process()]}.
608: enable_trace(Procs, Options) when Procs =:= processes; Procs =:= new_processes; Procs =:= existing_processes ->
609:     erlang:trace(Procs, true, trace_options(Options));
610: enable_trace({Children, PidOrName}, Options) when Children =:= children; Children =:= all_children ->
611:     Pids = children(Children, PidOrName),
612:     toggle_trace(Pids, true, trace_options(Options), 0, []);
613: enable_trace(Pid, Options) when is_pid(Pid); is_atom(Pid) ->
614:     toggle_process_trace(Pid, true, trace_options(Options));
615: enable_trace(List, Options) when is_list(List) ->
616:     toggle_trace(List, true, trace_options(Options), 0, []).
617: 
618: -doc """
619: The same as
620: [`disable_trace` ](`disable_trace/2`)`(Spec, #{set_on_spawn => true})`.
621: """.
622: -doc(#{since => <<"OTP @OTP-18756@">>}).
623: -spec disable_trace(Spec) -> non_neg_integer()
624:     when Spec :: pid() |
625:         processes |
626:         new_processes |
627:         existing_processes |
628:         {children | all_children, process()};
629:     ([process()]) -> non_neg_integer() | {non_neg_integer(), [process()]}.
630: disable_trace(Rootset) ->
631:     disable_trace(Rootset, #{set_on_spawn => true}).

633: -doc """
634: Stops accumulating traces for specified processes. See `enable_trace/2` for
635: options description.
636: 
637: Profile accumulated before process is removed from the traced list is retained.
638: This allows to enable tracing for many or even all processes in the system,
639: sleep for a short period of time, then disable tracing for all processes,
640: avoiding system overload, but keeping profile data.
641: """.
642: -doc(#{since => <<"OTP @OTP-18756@">>}).
643: -spec disable_trace(Spec, trace_options()) -> non_neg_integer()
644:     when Spec :: pid() |
645:         processes |
646:         new_processes |
647:         existing_processes |
648:         {children | all_children, process()};
649:     ([process()], trace_options()) -> non_neg_integer() | {non_neg_integer(), [process()]}.
650: disable_trace(Procs, Options) when Procs =:= processes; Procs =:= new_processes; Procs =:= existing_processes ->
651:     erlang:trace(Procs, false, trace_options(Options));
652: disable_trace({Children, PidOrName}, Options) when Children =:= children; Children =:= all_children ->
653:     Pids = children(Children, PidOrName),

656:     toggle_process_trace(Pid, false, trace_options(Options));
657: disable_trace(List, Options) when is_list(List) ->
658:     toggle_trace(List, false, trace_options(Options), 0, []).

764: -doc """
765: Produces ad-hoc profile for function `Fun` or `Module`:`Function` call. By
766: default, result is formatted to the output device, use `report` option to change
767: this behaviour.
768: 
769: Ad-hoc profiling starts a new instance of `tprof` server, runs the profiling
770: routine, extracts results and shuts the server down. If `tprof` is already
771: running (for server-aided profiling), default ad-hoc profiler options block this
772: call to avoid mixing results from several independent instances. Use
773: `registered => false` option to override this behaviour.
774: 
775: Ad-hoc profiler supports following`Options`:
776: 
777: - **`type`** - The type of profiling to perform.
778: 
779: - **`device`** - Specifies I/O devices to print the profile to. Useful to
780:   redirect text output to console or `standard_error`.
781: 
782: - **`pattern`** - Specifies trace pattern, or a list of trace patterns to
783:   enable. By default, all functions (`{'_', '_', '_'}`) are traced.
784: 
785: - **`registered`** - Specifies `tprof` registered process name. Use `false` to
786:   leave the process unregistered, or `{local, myname}` to register the process
787:   under a different name.
788: 
789: - **`report`** - Controls output format. The default is `process`, printing
790:   per-process profiling data sorted by percentage of the total allocation.
791:   Specify `report => return` to suppress printing and get the raw data for
792:   further evaluation with `inspect/3` and formatting with `format/2`.
793: 
794: - **`rootset`** - Includes extra processes in the trace list. Useful for
795:   profiling allocations for `m:gen_server`, calls, or other allocations caused
796:   by inter-process communications. See [example](`m:tprof#pg_example`).
797: 
798: - **`set_on_spawn`** - Automatically start tracing for processes spawned by the
799:   traced process. On by default.
800: 
801: - **`timeout`** - Terminate profiling after the specified amount of time
802:   (milliseconds).
803: """.
804: -doc(#{since => <<"OTP @OTP-18756@">>}).
805: -spec profile(module(), Fun :: atom(), Args :: [term()], profile_options()) -> ok | {term(), [trace_info()]}.
806: profile(Module, Function, Args, Options) when is_atom(Module), is_atom(Function), is_list(Args) ->
807:     do_profile({Module, Function, Args}, Options).

811: -record(tprof_state, {
812:     type = call_count :: trace_type(),
813:     trace_map = #{} :: trace_map(),
814:     paused = false :: boolean(),
815:     ad_hoc = undefined :: undefined |
816:         {pid(), Timer :: reference() | false, Patterns :: [trace_pattern()],
817:             RootSet :: rootset(), ReplyTo :: gen_server:from()}

825:     Type = maps:get(type, Config, call_count),
